title: Unified sync/async streaming chat: context-manager API, resumable checkpoints, and backpressure ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: SDK users need a single, ergonomic interface that works both sync and async for streaming chat completions, while supporting resumable sessions (after network blips), explicit checkpoint tokens for deterministic resumes, and backpressure controls to avoid unbounded memory growth in long-running streams. Current patterns in examples are fragmented: some users use callbacks, others use raw event loops or ad-hoc generators; resumability is inconsistent across handlers; retries lead to duplicate events or out-of-order application state when resuming.

Goals:
- Provide a context-manager-friendly API that is identical for sync and async usage (with minimal mental overhead).
- Support resumable checkpoints (opaque resume_token) that are produced at well-defined boundaries (message-complete, or after N tokens) and can be used to continue a stream without replaying duplicate content.
- Expose backpressure primitives (max_buffered_events, awaitable drain points) so high-throughput consumers can control memory & latency.
- Define deterministic deduplication rules and idempotent resume semantics (server-side and SDK-enforced) so resumed sessions cannot corrupt application state.

Non-goals: full redesign of streaming protocol or server changes; we will iterate with what server already emits and add SDK-side adaptations where necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Add a unified API: ChatStream (sync) and AsyncChatStream (async) that both implement __enter__/__exit__ and async context manager semantics respectively, and expose same methods: .events(), .checkpoint(), .resume(resume_token)
SDK will emit deterministic resume_token values at stable boundaries; resume(resume_token) must continue from that token without duplicating already-delivered final-message events
Backpressure controls: constructor accepts max_buffered_events and provides an awaitable .drain() that blocks producers when buffer is full
Retries: transient network errors call into the resume flow automatically once, with exponential backoff; user-visible hook for custom retry policy
Complete unit + integration tests covering resume, dedupe, and backpressure under high-concurrency (CI test harness simulates packet loss and delayed fragments)
Documentation + two runnable examples (sync and async) in examples/streaming_resume and examples/streaming_backpressure
Design doc and API surface reviewed and approved by SDK lead and API stability owner (PRD link in artifacts)
implementation_notes: High-level API shape: provide a builder pattern ChatStream.open(request, *, max_buffered_events=1024, checkpoint_interval_tokens=64, retry_policy=None)

Internals: maintain an ordered event buffer with sequence numbers from server; checkpoint token will be last-applied-seq + ephemeral session-id; on resume send last-applied-seq to server (if server supports), otherwise SDK will request server to replay starting from that seq and drop duplicates based on seq numbers

Backpressure: when buffer len >= max_buffered_events, suspend reading from socket (asyncio: await pause_reading coroutine; sync: block read loop) and resume when .drain() reduces buffer below threshold
Retries: add a helper RetryCoordinator that attempts one auto-resume for transient socket errors; if it fails, escalate error to user with guidance to retry manually with resume_token
Edge cases: partial tokens split across frames: coalesce fragments until complete event boundary before emitting; checkpoint only at message-complete or after checkpoint_interval_tokens
Type hints and stub files to keep mypy happy (we need both sync/async overloads).
Testing: reuse existing streaming test harness used by ENG-31247 but extend fault injection to close connection mid-message and validate resume semantics
design_decisions: Opted for SDK-side deduplication (seq-number based) instead of requiring server changes to maintain faster rollout and backward compatibility
Expose 'checkpoint_interval_tokens' as an ergonomic knob; default 64 balances latency and resume granularity
Unified API surface (ChatStream / AsyncChatStream) rather than a single coroutine that returns an iterator to make context-managed lifetime explicit
Make automatic resume conservative: one auto-attempt only to avoid hiding persistent server misconfigurations from users
open_questions: Should resume_token be opaque string or structured JSON with seq+session_id? (current plan: opaque string to support server-side flexibility)
If server-side resume is unavailable, SDK will ask server to replay and SDK will dedupe using seq numbers — do we need admin-visible telemetry to signal increased cost to customers?
Do we need a per-tenant toggle for automatic resume behavior until server-side protocol guarantees are stable?
progress_updates: 2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket and drafted API sketch. Linked to prototype experiment in notebooks/stream-resume-experiment.ipynb.

2026-03-07 - Claire Huang: Implemented initial AsyncChatStream prototype that yields Event objects with seq. Basic checkpoint token generation and resume call implemented (internal branch: feat/stream-resume).

2026-03-09 - Review: API review with SDK team. Feedback: avoid exposing raw seq numbers publicly; switch to opaque tokens. Also request explicit backpressure awaitable instead of implicit blocking in sync API.

2026-03-11 - Thomas Becker (infra): Added CI fault-injection harness to simulate TCP drop mid-chunk. Found duplicate final tokens after resume — root cause: server replay behavior + SDK previously emitted pre-checkpoint partial event. Patch created to coalesce fragments before emitting (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/pull/2567).

2026-03-13 - Claire Huang: WIP: implemented .drain() awaitable and sync-blocking counterpart. Added integration tests for resume dedupe (tests/stream_resume_test.py). CI tests failing intermittently on Windows runners — flakiness investigation opened (ENG-42112).
notes_for_reviewers: Please evaluate the proposed public API and the trade-offs in 'design_decisions'. The core ask is to keep resume semantics deterministic without server changes if possible.

Pay attention to the backpressure ergonomics for the sync API: we currently block reader thread when buffer is full; alternatives discussed include callback-based flow control or exposing a blocking producer interface.
Security: checkpoint tokens are opaque but may include session ids; we should confirm token entropy & rotation with secops before GA (cc: security team).
